title: Buzz wire: carry the ring along a bent wire without touching it
instruction: Move the metal ring from the green starting point to the red endpoint along the wire without allowing the ring to touch the wire.
context: The buzz-wire game tests continuous, collision-free motion of a held tool along a 3D path, as in guiding a tool through a constrained space. The wire bends a quarter turn each way and climbs and drops, so the ring has to be turned on the way: no fixed orientation gets it through.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. A 1 cm wooden base (25.5 x 25.1 cm) is taped to the table centred at x 25.3, y -0.4. A 3 mm steel wire, 34.3 cm long, runs 6 cm up from a post at x 15, y 0: straight away from the robot to x 20 under a green insulating sleeve (7 mm, first 3.5 cm), a quarter turn to the robot's left climbing to 9.2 cm (x 24.5, y 7), a half turn back to the right, dropping (x 28, y 4.6), a quarter turn to the left at 6 cm (x 28.3, y 0), and straight away from the robot to a post at x 35.5, y -4 under a red sleeve (last 3 cm). Its exact path is in track.py and wire_path.csv. A steel ring (24 mm inside, 30 mm outside, 3 mm thick) with a 70 x 10 x 10 mm handle, 20 g together, sits around the wire at x 17 over the green sleeve, its axis along the wire, its bottom in a 5 mm groove on a wooden stand and its handle level, pointing to the robot's right, its end on a wooden rest.
scoring: Measured through the run by the scorer (in the real build: a low-voltage continuity circuit between ring and bare wire). Checkpoints at 20, 40, 60, 80 % of the bare wire between the sleeves score 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 when the ring passes them in order, and 1.0 when it reaches the red sleeve; credit counts only until the ring first touches the bare wire (the sleeves do not count), and credit earned before the touch is kept. Full score also needs the ring resting at the red sleeve for 1 s.
reset_notes: Slide the ring back along the wire to the green sleeve (it cannot come off the wire) and set its bottom in the stand's groove and its handle on the rest.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The wire is fixed: a chain of 3 mm capsules every 6 mm along a smooth spline, 7 mm under the sleeves. The ring is 24 straight 3 x 3 mm chords of the circle plus its handle, one free body (friction 0.6). A touch is the ring's centre line coming within 3 mm of the bare wire's, measured every step. Checked in PyBullet (check_physics.py): the ring rests on its stand clear of the wire, and the wire traps it.
